# 1 Enoch Chapter 24 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Watchers

---

**1** From there I traveled to another region of the earth where I was shown a range of mountains burning with fire that never went out, day or night.

**2** I went on past those mountains and saw seven magnificent peaks, each one different from the rest. The stones were stunning and beautiful — glorious in appearance, flawless on the outside.

**3** Three of the mountains rose up toward the east, each one built on top of the one before it; three more rose toward the south, also stacked upon one another, with deep jagged ravines between them, none of them connecting.

**4** The seventh mountain stood at the center of all the others, rising higher than any of them, shaped like the base of a throne. Fragrant trees surrounded it on every side.

**5** Among those trees was one unlike anything I had ever encountered. Nothing else I had smelled was like it. Its fragrance surpassed every other fragrance in existence. Its leaves, blossoms, and wood never wither — not ever. Its fruit was lovely, resembling the dates of a palm tree.

**6** I exclaimed: "What a beautiful tree this is! How stunning it looks!" Then Raphael, the holy angel beside me, answered:

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 24 is the first part of the great tree-of-life vision. The seven mountains arranged around a central throne-peak evoke the cosmic geography of divine dwelling. The extraordinary fragrant tree's eternal qualities — undying leaves, blossoms, and wood — signal its supernatural status. Raphael's interrupted speech continues in ch. 25.*
